title: Sir Thomas Urquhart's Cyphral Octastich (The Jewel, 1652) and Cyphral Distich

system.summary: Book cipher on the book itself: number n at position k gives the initial of the first word beginning with the needed letter, found as word n of physical page k of The Jewel (1652).
system.notes: System is for the octastich; the distich's construction is not established.

prior_solution.where: Vals AI, 31 Aug 2026, same rule and plaintext for the octastich; distich claim also published

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: first-occurrence test with shuffled and random-page controls

solution.what: Provenance objection checked on the 1653 scan and Wilcock 1899.
Octastich measured on Schmeh's 272 numbers and called a book cipher by shape; judged unattackable without the key text.
The poem names its key text (Exskybalauron): number k indexes a word on physical page k of The Jewel.
DP alignment of Schmeh's defective 272 numbers against TCP pages.
Straight decode one number per physical page: 238/284 first-occurrence hits.
Shuffled numbers and random page orders give 0.43 (max 0.51).
Distich Proquiritation rule: 34/64 hits, chance, no English; page-index variants also at chance.
Line 5 numbers re-checked on the 1983 photograph at full resolution, and the other gap positions on both photographs. Numbers identical to ct.py; the residual misses are not transcription errors.

Line 5 re-segmented: tail 163-177 fixes (u)surpd authoritie, 150-157 give OVERTHRO, 158 W on the TCP gap page, 159-161 HIS (TCP 'Leopoldo s' phantom token explains 161). 'And [?] overthrow his usurp'd authoritie'.
Old 0.788 counted any decoded letter; new measure_sense.py counts exact or within-2 first-occurrence support for the reading's letter: octastich 274/285 = 0.961, overall with distich 274/349 = 0.785.
Distich as word indices into the octastich reading and the Decagram verse (alone and concatenated).

Fetched the 1834 Works text; distich as word- and letter-index keys into the six-line verse, Parva peto couplet (Latin and English), octastich reading and Decagram verse, alone and concatenated both orders: 76 decodes, best -6.76/char vs -5.09 English.

outcome.method_basis: The octastich is a book cipher on The Jewel (1652) itself: word n on physical page k, first word with the needed initial. Vals AI published this rule and plaintext on 31 Aug 2026, before this attempt, and the project verified it against the EEBO-TCP text using a fresh transcription of the numbers.

gaps.detail: 1652 leaves needed: p. 149 word 2 gives C where a one-letter word is required; the leaf counted as p. 158 is a gap in the TCP
numbers confirmed on the 1983 photographs; writer's or compositor's slips, letter fixed by context only

claimed Proquiritation rule gives 34/64, chance; page-index variants on The Jewel and Logopandecteision at chance; key text not identified; verse, Parva peto couplet and octastich texts as word/letter-index keys also at noise (5 Oct 2026)

outcome.notes: Octastich read (0.961 measured as sense): line 5 re-read 5 Oct 2026 as 'And [?] overthrow his usurp'd authoritie'; 11 positions are slips or TCP gaps. Distich (64 numbers) unread, so the target stays read in part.
outcome.fraction_read_source: measure_sense.py / measure_sense.txt: octastich 274 of 285 positions read as sense (233 exact, 41 within 2 words of the first occurrence); distich 64 unread; 274/349
